definitions.gloss: good luck, do your best, hang in there
definitions.explanation: An expression of encouragement. It comes from the verb {頑張|がんば}る (to persevere, to do one's best). Used to cheer someone on.

examples.japanese: ⟦{試験|しけん}→試験：01422_shiken⟧、{頑張|がんば}って！
{頑張|がんば}って⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
⟦もう→もう：00602_mou⟧⟦{少|すこ}し→少し：00596_sukoshi⟧⟦だから→だから：00924_dakara⟧、{頑張|がんば}って！
examples.english: Just a little more, hang in there!

examples.japanese: ⟦{明日|あした}→明日：00501_ashita⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{試合|しあい}→試合：01601_shiai⟧、{頑張|がんば}って⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧。⟦{応援|おうえん}→応援：01900_ouen⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧。
examples.english: Good luck in tomorrow's game. I'm cheering for you.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{仕事|しごと}→仕事：00480_shigoto⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{疲|つか}れていた→疲れる：00901_tsukareru⟧⟦けど→けど：09477_kedo⟧、{頑張|がんば}って⟦{最後|さいご}→最後：01413_saigo⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦やり{遂|と}げました→やり遂げる：noentry⟧。
examples.english: He was tired from work, but he persevered and finished it to the end.

notes: {頑張|がんば}って is the te-form of {頑張|がんば}る used as an expression of encouragement. It's very commonly used before tests, competitions, or any challenging situation. The polite form is {頑張|がんば}ってください. Note that in Western culture 'good luck' implies chance, but {頑張|がんば}って implies effort and perseverance.
